exclude: DCS introduction and exit wrapper. The game enters at $4000.
Live VIC character window. The hand-over still holds the DCS font from $7000. The authored factory set at $7800 is tracked separately.

comments.text: 96 consecutive 64-byte VIC sprite slots in the factory arrangement. The laboratory transition swaps this whole window with $E000–$F7FF.
Shape pointers $90–$9F in the factory sprite window. The neutral airborne pose uses the pair $9C and $9D in sprite slots 1 and 2 at $417D and $4182.
Shape pointers $A0–$AF. The shared factory pickup image is pointer $AE, assigned to slots 0 and 5 by $639C.
Shape pointers $B0–$BF. The factory raster routine at $6134 sets $B0 for sprite 3 and $B1 for sprite 4.
Shape pointers $C0–$CF. Down plus fire selects the $CF and $CE pair for one facing at $446D.
Shape pointers $D0–$DF in the last quarter of the factory VIC sprite window. Saved under the KERNAL at $F400 on laboratory entry.
The VIC reads the live character set here. The hand-over still shows the intro font copied from $7000, before $408B replaces it with the factory set from $7800.

Disable the VIC interrupt, install the KERNAL IRQ hook, resume CIA timing and configure multicolour text at $0400. A lab return takes the restore path at $40BA. A fresh run resets room, pickup and lab state and copies the factory character set before the lift sequence.
Set room offset zero, initialise 50 per-floor pickup flags to $FF, clear the shared lab state and set energy to $FF before installing the factory character set.
Copy eight pages from $7800 to $3800, then set up the agent sprites and pass the initial five-byte lift record to $6078.
Reinitialise agent sprites and restore the saved factory room, floor, horizontal position and energy before dispatching the room.
Zero $D400–$D418 inclusive.
Snapshot of bit 4 of $DC00. Zero means fire is held.
Index into the directional movement sprite pointer tables.
The sign distinguishes left-facing from right-facing poses.
Nonzero in the low pose. The sign records the facing at entry. Horizontal crawling can change the live facing at $40D9.
Zero selects the upper floor. Nonzero selects the lower floor for elevator, collision and pickup logic.
Nonzero requests a single energy decrement at $41E3. The redraw at $64AF clears it.
Set to $FF when the factory energy renderer writes no filled cells. The main loop tests it before taking input.
Nonzero sends the main loop to the lift transition at $5DC1.

Refresh the player's composite sprite. Give energy loss and pending lift entry priority over contact checks and joystick dispatch. The movement branches converge at $41D6, where an active lift bypasses the ordinary updates.
Read active-low port 2 controls. Save fire separately and dispatch up, down, left and right in that order, subject to movement state.
Reset the walking frame and choose stationary sprite pointers for the active facing and pose. Fire can enter the action branches at $4985 or $4A00.
Route lift animation to $5F28 while active. Otherwise consume pending damage, run the update routines and return to the main loop.
Eighty tile codes copied across two screen rows by $4242, with colour $08.
Write part of the room's tile layout and set the corresponding colour cells to $08 through the screen and colour pointers.
Configure the two player sprite slots, shared multicolour values and starting coordinates.
Four shape pointers for the first player layer during upward animation.
Four shape pointers for the second layer, selected alongside the table at $4393.
Reverse the low pose when crawling. Otherwise advance a timed upward sprite sequence with paired shape pointers and a sound request.
Throttle the down action with $4442. With fire held while upright, set the crawl state and move the player sprite down $15 pixels.
Select left-facing pointers and dispatch the low-pose branch when crawling. Use $4538 as a movement and animation divider.
Right-facing movement and sprite animation. Its frame tables supply both halves of the agent sprite.
Count down the divider bytes at $468A and $468B before setting positive vertical movement state. The update uses pose and Y-delta tables.
Use the left-facing vertical movement path from the signed state at $40DB. Advance the player layers using the paired animation tables in this section.
Route the signed facing to left or right movement. The horizontal step loop updates the composite player position and uses room dispatch when it crosses the room boundary.
Copy the primary player sprite's position to the second layer so the two sprite shapes move together.
Use two countdowns to pace the pickup animation. Update the sprite pointer fields after the inner phase reaches zero.
Count down $4975 before advancing the positive $40DC action state. The animation applies a Y offset, aligns the other player sprite and reads paired shape tables.
Count down $49F0 before advancing the negative $40DC action. The left-facing tables advance together and the last frame clears the action.
Choose left-facing crawl pointers and use the shared horizontal movement engine. This path changes current facing without replacing the recorded crawl-facing byte.
Choose right-facing crawl pointers and use the shared horizontal movement engine. Entry-facing information remains in $40DD.
Copy a run of tiles to the screen pointer, advancing the pointer across page boundaries.
Five tile codes used on alternating rows by the tall factory fixture renderer.
Five tile codes for the second row of each repeated pair in the tall fixture.
Five tile codes copied immediately after the ten repeating fixture rows.
The last five positions of the fixture. Zero leaves an existing cell untouched.
Draw a five-column decoration at the screen pointer in $57, alternating two row patterns five times and appending two cap rows. Zero in the last pattern leaves that cell intact.
Add 40 to the screen pointer at $57–$58.
Thirty codes used by $4BA3 when $4BA2 is zero, arranged as six rows of five.
The alternate door's thirty codes, used by $4BA3 when $4BA2 is nonzero.
Draw a five-cell by six-row rectangle at $57. Use $4B83 when $4BA2 is set and $4B65 otherwise, then clear the selector.
Draw the fifth laboratory entrance room, mark its left boundary and configure the two door positions and lift record at offset $32.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $2A. The setup first calls $50D7. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Copy two rows of nine cells from $4CDE to the screen pointer in $57. Leave cells with zero source codes intact.
Even byte offset into the 25-entry room dispatch table. Each room change advances or backs up by two.
Room routines use $01 to block backward travel and $FF to block forward travel in the dispatcher.
Two-byte working destination loaded from the room dispatch table immediately before the indirect jump.
Advance the room offset by two unless the current room marks the right boundary, then dispatch the new room.
Retreat the room offset by two unless the current room marks the left boundary, then dispatch the new room.
Load a little-endian address from $4D62 indexed by the room byte offset and jump through $4D2D.
25 little-endian room setup addresses. The index is a byte offset and increases by two per room.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $2C. The setup first calls $50D7. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $2E. The setup first calls $50D7. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $30. The setup first calls $56A3. Its code selects lift record offsets $37, $5A. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Draw a standard room with pickups, place both doors, set laboratory selection to 1 and select the first five-byte lift record.
Reset sprite visibility, draw the factory wall and floor layers, redraw the energy display and place recurring room decorations.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $0A. The setup first calls $4F34. Its code selects lift record offsets $0F, $14. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $14. The setup first calls $4F34. Its code selects lift record offset $2D. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $1E. The setup first calls $4F34. Its code selects lift record offsets $50, $4B. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $02. The setup first calls $50D7. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $04. The setup first calls $50D7. Its code selects lift record offset $1E. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $06. The setup first calls $50D7. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $0C. The setup first calls $50D7. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $0E. The setup first calls $50D7. Its code selects lift record offset $19. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $10. The setup first calls $50D7. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $16. The setup first calls $50D7. Its code selects lift record offset $41. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $18. The setup first calls $50D7. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $1A. The setup first calls $50D7. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $20. The setup first calls $50D7. Its code selects lift record offset $46. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $22. The setup first calls $50D7. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $24. The setup first calls $50D7. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $08. The setup first calls $56A3. Its code selects lift record offsets $05, $23. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $12. The setup first calls $56A3. Its code selects lift record offset $0A. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $1C. The setup first calls $56A3. Its code selects lift record offsets $3C, $28. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Set up factory room with dispatch offset $26. The setup first calls $56A3. Its code selects lift record offset $55. It passes coordinates to the pickup sprite routine at $639C.
Advance the two dividers and copy the next group of 16 bytes from $57EF into the live glyph set at $3F60.
Copy three rows of four codes from $5842 onward. Zero leaves the destination unchanged.
Use $589F as a divider, set a two-pixel move and select the direction from the active floor's configuration.
After both timers expire, copy 16 bytes of the next animation phase from $58D4 into character data at $3938. Set $5917 on the last phase.
Preserve the player sprite layers while clearing the room-specific visibility bits.
Read the VIC background collision latch for sprites 1 and 2. Select a minimum player Y by floor before invoking the position-dependent checks.

Read the sprite collision latch. Contact including the player group and sprite 5 enters the pickup path, adds up to eight energy units and clears the room-floor pickup flag. Another contact branch decrements energy if $60E4 is set.
Combine the latched background collision with the active floor, sprite X high bit and room flags to decide if the player is inside a damage interval.
Add the current $5970 offset to the X threshold in A.
Count down $59E0 and reload it to $10 before setting the damage request.
Set $40DF to $FF for the energy update later in the main loop.
Jump to the routine that stores the pending factory energy decrement.
Use the active floor and horizontal position to choose a contact interval. When there is no qualifying collision, restore the default collision offset at $5B36.
Restore the shared X adjustment used by the collision intervals and foreground priority logic.
Divert the upper floor contact handler to the paced damage path at $5A76.
When the room and floor permit it, test the player X range against four room feature flags. A qualifying contact can route to the timed damage request at $5A76.
Enter the handler that sets the lift request flag at $40E1.
Test room-specific flags for the active floor and compare the player sprite X against the lift entrance interval. A matching position can request the transition.
Keep the player sprite visible as the display changes, increment both sprite Y registers until sprite 1 reaches $FC, clear movement state and return to the intro or to the saved lab exit vector.
Unsigned energy shared with the lab through $BFF7. A fresh attempt starts at $FF.
Seven screen codes copied to the first screen row by $5D7B.
Set top-row colours, copy seven caption cells into $0400 and refresh the energy gauge with a decrement followed by an increment.
Select lift state from the current floor. Where enabled, clear the display, initialise lift sprites and use the phase data starting at $5DB2.
Continue the lift loop through $5F17 while the lift flag routes the factory loop here.

Clear the active lift flags, restore the ordinary IRQ vector and copy destination room, floor and X from the lift record. Dispatch the destination room unless the completed-game exit condition is met.
Acknowledge VIC raster interrupts during the lift. Set a sound request and dispatch by the phase byte at $5DB2. Other IRQs use the saved default vector at $40C5.
Twenty five-byte records copied into $5DB2–$5DB6 by the transition setup. Room code supplies a byte offset into this table.
Copy five bytes from $6014+Y into $5DB2 and mark both floor lift flags.
Save room offset, floor and player X, transfer energy to $BFF7 and jump into the already resident program at $8000.
If the lab return flag is set, restore room offset, floor, X and shared energy. Choose Y=$6B or $CB for the saved floor and clear the return flag.
Point the KERNAL IRQ hook at $611A, select raster line 257 and enable the VIC raster interrupt. Clear $60E4 before returning.
Handle the room's raster event, starting with VIC acknowledgement and the $60E4 state test. Non-raster interrupts chain to the factory sound IRQ vector.
Every fifth call, move the Y byte at $60EC by one. The direction flips at $DB on the rising-value leg and below $BB on the falling-value leg.
Fifty per-floor flags. The room offset picks the first of the two flags and floor selects which one to clear on pickup.
Use two coordinate pairs in $57–$5A and the per-floor flags to place and enable pickup sprite slots 0 and 5. Their order is swapped on the lower floor.
Increment energy and redraw unless energy is already $FF.
Decrement the energy byte and fall through to the gauge renderer.
Set the sound request, copy energy to the shared byte and render complete eight-unit cells followed by any partial cell. Raise $40E0 if no cells were filled and clear the pending damage flag.
Eight-page source copied to VIC character memory at $3800 on a new attempt. It carries both room tiles and the glyphs used in the top row.
Factory character patterns $80–$FF, copied to $3C00–$3FFF. The rendered ENERGY caption uses codes $85, $8E, $92, $87 and $99 in this half.
Configure multicolour text, install the laboratory return vector for the death sequence, clear screen and colour RAM, swap in laboratory art and initialise layout, shared energy and floor selection.
Bank out the KERNAL and exchange all 6144 bytes at $2000–$37FF with RAM at $E000–$F7FF. Restore the KERNAL before returning.
Bank out the KERNAL and exchange $0800–$0FFF with RAM at $F800–$FFFF. This moves 2048 bytes per call.
Swap both graphics windows back before jumping to the intro entry used by this release.
Forty-five tile codes at the initial pointer $8127. $8177 reads them in five rows of nine.
Draw three five-row machine blocks and write single-cell details to screen and colour RAM.
Copy a 9 by 5 tile rectangle. The source starts at the pointer in $8127 and the destination starts at $57. Destination rows are 40 cells apart.
Forty tile codes copied to the first floor strip beginning at $04F0.
Forty tile codes copied to the second floor strip at $05E0.
Forty tile codes copied to the third floor strip at $06D0.
Forty tile codes copied to the fourth floor strip at $07C0.
Copy four 40-cell floor strips from $81AF, $81D7, $81FF and $8227 to their fixed screen rows.
Draw two seven by five rectangles at screen addresses $0449 and $0629. Then continue with the four by four decoration.
Copy four rows of four tiles from the pointer at $8357 to screen RAM beginning at $0431, then continue with the next decoration.
Write five codes from $849C down the screen starting at $053F, then call $84E5 for details at $0608 and $071E.
Current laboratory energy. Initialised from $BFF7 and kept in sync by the lab gauge renderer.
Seven screen codes copied to the first screen row by $8605.
Set the seven label cells' colour to 5, the remaining row to colour 2 and copy the caption to screen RAM before calling the lab gauge update.
Prioritise special states, then process ongoing energy drain and the laboratory entities before polling port 2 for ordinary movement.
Read active-low port 2 for movement and fire. Store the raw fire bit at $8658 then dispatch up, down, left and right in order.
Continue the laboratory update with the active laboratory number from $BFF6.
For a cleared laboratory, skip the entity update sequence. Wait on $873D when the movement flag at $865E is clear.
Handle left joystick input with the lab movement divider, facing and animation state before updating the current sprite and position.
Handle right joystick input. Its own sprite pointer table and timing state select the corresponding walking poses.
Wait for $8881, then advance the negative $865C movement and its sprite-Y and shape sequences. Continue through the horizontal limit handler while the sequence is active.
Time the positive $865C move with $88E3. Its sequence writes sprite 1 Y and pointer, then either resets the movement state or applies the boundary test.
Rate-limit the directional action with $8929 and advance the frame at $8659. Nonterminal frames route to the horizontal limits with the action step size.
Time this action with $8962 and enter the horizontal limit check using the matching sprite sequence.
Use $89B7 to time the negative $865D animation. Update the player's Y and shape and clear $865D when the sequence ends.
Time the positive $865D sequence with $8A14. Advance the sprite position and pose without the horizontal limit handler.
Select limits from player facing, the ninth X bit, floor and movement flags before choosing the next position and motion state.
Install lab raster vector $8C2A using $8B1E, choose line $32 and enable raster interrupts.
Pass non-raster interrupts to the sound handler. For VIC interrupts select one of five bands by raster position. Four bands reload a floor's sprite records and the fifth sets up the next frame.
Write the active floor record through a pointer in $FB. Preserve the player position fields and ninth X bit while updating other sprite coordinates, attributes, colours and shape pointers.
Load the record pointer at $8B46, apply it to the sprite registers and set the next raster interrupt to line $90.
Apply the record selected by $8B48 and schedule line $C0 for the next band.
Apply the final floor record selected by $8B4A, then schedule line zero.
At the frame wrap, schedule line $32 for the first floor record of the next frame.
Advance the periodic machine animation. When its secondary counter expires outside the blocked state, set any of the four inactive assistant flags back to its active value.
Use $8E23 to enable the first entrance sequence and $8E24 to pace it. Write coordinates at $8B56–$8B57 and enable the next movement phase through $90A3.
Pace the second entrance with $8E82. Advance the coordinates at $8B8D–$8B8E through its horizontal limits and hand off to $9133.
When the $8EEA entrance flag is set, step the third entity's coordinates toward Y=$B3 and hand off to $91D5.
When $8F3D enables this sequence, use the divider at $8F3E to step the fourth entity toward Y=$D8 and hand off to $9265.
Advance the two countdowns and issue the $C014 sound request when the animation reaches its update path.
Copy the current frame from the graphics source at $3D50 to glyph storage at $3B78 after both dividers expire.
Use the phase at $9003 to copy a frame from $3D08 to glyph storage at $3A50.
Use the phase at $9039 to copy a frame from $3D20 to glyph storage at $3A10.
Use the phase at $906F to copy a frame from $3D38 to glyph storage at $3B70.
Pace changes to the first entity record with $90A4 and cycle the shape at $8B7F up to the boundary value $C3.
When $9133 is set and $9134 expires, cycle the second record's shape at $8BB6 using $C6 as the upper check.
When $91D5 is set, use the divider at $91D6 before testing the third entity's pointer at $8BED against $C9.
Use $9265 to gate the update and $9266 to pace the animation. Compare $8C24 with $CC before changing the last record's pointer.
When $92F4 is nonzero, pace updates with $92F5. Its sign chooses the movement direction and $92F7–$92F8 select the special motion branches.
Use $93CF to step through the first assistant's turn sequence at $93BD. Store each new pointer at $8B7D, then clear the turn flag and reverse its direction.
Update the first assistant's shape pointer through the $9407 index. Clear its pose flag on reaching the final frame.
Use the second assistant's active direction and timing flags at $942B–$942F for its corresponding movement sequence.
Step the second assistant's turn frame through $9506 and write $8BB4. Finish by clearing the turn flag and changing the signed direction field.
Update the second assistant's shape through $9532, then clear its pose flag at $942F.
Run the third assistant's timed movement using $9556–$955A. That group includes the flag checked when the lab tests completion.
Step through the third assistant's turn sequence using $9631. Update shape $8BEB and resolve the turn flag and direction at the end.
Use $965D to advance the third assistant's shape and clear $955A when the pose sequence finishes.
Advance the bottom floor assistant with flags at $9681–$9685. A cleared first flag also counts as an inactive assistant at $9CE3.
Update the bottom assistant's shape at $8C22 through sequence index $975C, then clear the turn flag and update the direction.
Write the bottom assistant shape through the $9788 index and clear $9685 at the end of the sequence.
Select a coordinate test using the current floor number and the player's ninth X bit. A qualifying gap can set $8662 to trigger a fall. The bottom-left exit test can lead to $9CE3.
Select alternating $8B and $8C sprite pointers through two divider bytes and use the floor and sprite X to choose movement or the branch that consumes one unit of energy.
Select $8F and $90 sprite pointers and test the left-side thresholds before moving again or clearing the recoil state and consuming energy.
Set the joystick-change threshold to four plus lab number, select encounter duration from the lab and floor, suspend that assistant's movement and enter the encounter loop.
Compare the entire CIA port byte with the previous sample. Count byte transitions, then recharge when the count reaches the threshold. With fewer transitions, a countdown can instead trigger damage.
Compare the input-change count to the current threshold, clear it when it reaches that threshold and call the capped energy increment at $9D45.
Decrement the encounter's energy countdown. On expiry, subtract one unit and reload the countdown to $80.
When both countdown gates expire, clear bit 6 of all four assistant records and clear the shared encounter and respawn-blocking state.
Every $20 inner ticks, increment player Y. After the fall counter expires, increment floor number and clear the falling flag.
Test four assistant flags. Only four zero values reach the store that marks this lab complete. Reset movement and assistant state before returning to the factory.
Increase lab energy unless it is already at the maximum. Continue to the gauge renderer after incrementing.
Subtract one from lab energy before updating the gauge and shared energy.
Count down $9DB1. If a fight is active, end that encounter first. Otherwise clear the special movement flags and jump through the stored death vector.
Set the return flag, preserve energy, check the five laboratory-status bytes and set the all-labs flag if they are all nonzero. Swap out laboratory graphics and jump to $4000.
Four consecutive 55-byte records copied into the lab entity state area before assistant movement begins.
Copy $DC bytes from the pointer at $9E18 to the pointer at $8B44, then initialise the active flags and effect counters.
Select one of five six-sprite sources by lab number. Values outside 1–5 return without copying through this routine.
Copy six consecutive 64-byte shapes to $31C0–$333F from the pointer supplied in A:Y.
Nonzero requests factory state restoration on entry at $4000.
Five laboratory completion bytes, checked in order by the lab return code.
Laboratory number 1–5, written by factory room setup and used by the lab layout and fight logic.
Energy passed from factory to laboratory and back.
Set during lab return when the five completion bytes all pass their nonzero tests.
Restore the VIC memory setup and test the sound requests in priority order. The individual effects set SID registers and chain to KERNAL IRQ service.
Clear the seven voice 1 registers, set envelope and master volume, choose one of two frequency pairs and enable noise with gate.
Service the $C004 request. Start it through $C0E9 or count down $C005 before clearing its request and active flag.
Clear the voice 2 and 3 registers and configure the two voices, including the voice 3 envelope and frequency.
Service the $C00C request. If active, expire it through the $C00D divider and clear the request and active flag. Otherwise start it at $C149.
Clear the SID, set the voice 1 pulse width and envelope, use shared energy as the low frequency byte and start the gated effect.
Service the $C010 sound request. Start at $C1AB or use the divider at $C011 to clear the gate and both flags.
Initialise SID voice 2 with its envelope and preset frequency from $C1DF, then enable noise and gate.
Enter the $C014 sound handler. On expiry clear its request and active flag and write $10 to the voice 1 control register.
Clear voice 1, set its envelope and frequency, set filter routing to $F1 and start the gate.
Check the lift-effect active flag and stop the voice when its timer reaches zero. Continue into the remaining sound priority tests.
Reset voices 2 and 3, initialise voice 2 and write the gate and effect state before resuming other sound tests.
96 64-byte slots under the KERNAL. The lab transition exchanges this block with the VIC-visible sprite window at $2000.
Lab backing store for VIC shape pointers $90–$9F. When active, the facing-specific sequence at $99E8 toggles $8F and $90 for sprite 1.
Lab backing store for shape pointers $A0–$AF. The branch at $9DD3 returns sprite 1 to shape $A1.
Lab backing store for pointers $B0–$BF. The machine animation at $8DA6 cycles pointer values $BE through $C0.
Final $0800 bytes of the laboratory sprite exchange window. On first lab entry this range is exchanged with $3000–$37FF.
Lab backing store for shape pointers $D0–$DF. The fight animation cycles the four assistant shape fields from $D9 through $DC.
Two kilobytes of laboratory data held under the KERNAL and exchanged with $0800–$0FFF at the transition. Sprite copies for the five lab IDs read from this window after the swap.
Backing bytes for the laboratory's $0C00–$0FFF after the swap. Includes the six-shape sources for lab IDs 4 and 5 at active addresses $0D00 and $0E80.
